chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Zura'ah ibn Muhammad al-Hadrami and Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

Indeed, our God has protected our followers from six [characteristics]: that they may be greedy like a crow, or bark like dogs, or be gay, or have children born out of fornication, or have children born to them out of fornication, or go door-to-door to beg.

key_terms.يَتَصَدَّقُوا عَلَى الْأَبْوَابِ: they give charity at the doors (begging)

ai.seo_question: What are the six characteristics that God protects the Shia from according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifying six distinct moral and social vices from which true followers are divinely protected, emphasizing both internal character and external conduct. These traits—ranging from insatiable greed and foolish chatter to specific sexual deviances and the humiliation of begging—serve as markers of spiritual purity and dignity for the Shia community. This narration underscores the comprehensive nature of Shia ethics, linking personal piety with social behavior.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 6-38 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Zar’at ibn Muhammad al-Hazrami and Muhammad ibn Sin’an, on the authority of Al-Mufaz’zal ibn Umar that he had heard Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) say,

“Indeed the Honorable the Exalted God has protected our followers from the following six characteristics: being greedy like a crow; barking like a dog; being gay; being born out of fornication; having children born out of fornication; and going door to door to beg.”
